products.name: Automation Anywhere
products.note: Intelligent automation platform; AI-powered bots; control room governance; credential vault

reading.body:
Automation Anywhere is an enterprise software platform for intelligent automation founded in 2003 and headquartered in California. It combines AI-powered bots, robotic process automation, and agentic orchestration to automate mission-critical workflows.

The company positions itself around coordination of multiple automation types. Its Mozart Orchestrator mechanism is built to manage AI agents, deterministic automations, and human workers together in a single workflow. This modular approach matters because it treats AI agents as one tool among others rather than a replacement for existing enterprise automation logic. The platform includes governance controls and credential vaults, suggesting it addresses security and compliance concerns that arise when automation touches sensitive enterprise systems.

The use cases on Automation Anywhere's site center on IT service management, where the platform targets employee self-service, IT desk workload reduction, and incident prediction. This is a narrower scope than the marketing claim of "number one provider of agentic automation" indicates. The data does not reveal deployment scale, customer count, revenue, or whether the platform's compute demands are significant enough to influence data center or power consumption. The 181 California legal exposure entries reflect its headquarters location but offer no detail on the nature, status, or outcome of any legal matters.

profile_text.body:
Automation Anywhere is a California-based company founded in 2003 that describes itself as the number one provider of agentic automation. Its site presents an agentic process automation system that combines AI, automation, and robotic process automation to deliver what it calls secure end-to-end enterprise agentic automation for mission-critical processes. The company says its Mozart Orchestrator coordinates AI agents, deterministic automations, and people, and it offers a free Cloud Community Edition with full-featured automation access. It also points to a global partner network and lists uses including employee self-service, IT service desk workload reduction, incident prediction through AIOps, and cost reduction in ITSM.

The site frames the market skeptically, citing Gartner for the claim that more than 90% of so-called "agentic" AI solutions are repackaged generative AI layered atop legacy systems, with only around 130 vendors among thousands actually delivering genuine agent-driven orchestration. A customer testimonial on the page says the customer also explored Microsoft Power Automate but found it was not as mature or up to enterprise level at the time, and chose Automation Anywhere instead. The company states a commitment to responsible AI and human-centered principles.

Product information describes Automation Anywhere as an intelligent automation platform with AI-powered bots, control room governance, and a credential vault. Legal exposure is recorded for California, with a count of 281. No lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded.
